findings.title: Early interpolation defeats $__range no-split guard
findings.body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() before partitioning into splitting/non-splitting queries. querySupportsSplitting() explicitly excludes queries containing a range variable because interpolating $__range per split is wrong. If applyTemplateVariables replaces $__range/$__timeRange, the expr no longer contains the variable when querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable runs, so range-variable queries will now be split and each split will get a baked-in full-range value instead of being left unsplit.

findings.title: Range-dependent macros frozen to full range before time-splitting
findings.body: Interpolating at the start uses request.range/intervalMs for the whole time range. Split sub-requests later get smaller ranges with the already-interpolated expr/step (e.g. $__auto, $__interval, $__rate_interval). Those macros should be evaluated per split partition, not once upfront, otherwise step/interval baked from the full range is reused for every 1-day chunk.

findings.title: Template variables/filters applied twice in shard path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) and then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery(), which now interpolates again with the same scopedVars/filters. A second applyTemplateVariables pass can double-apply ad-hoc filters from request.filters and re-replace already interpolated expr/step, corrupting the sharded selector produced by interpolateShardingSelector.
